summary: Fresh bounded exact-source review found no substantive defect in the five frozen modules. The numerical substitution pays the actual natural collision factor; the dense branch retains a strictly positive real edge witness; the other branch is a genuine full covering bounded minor. Selected-host restriction and seeded degree regularization construct actual graphs and preserve the literal star family, full coverage, exact size ratio and original mate threshold under explicit premises.

scope.mode: Read all five exact production sources and relevant unchanged graph, packing, minor, mate-freeness and seeded-trimming dependencies. Independently hash all manifest entries, compare prior library files, inspect recorded gates and their scripts, and verify the source-context caveat against the locally supplied Postle source text. Write only this review report.

semantic_checks.topic: CleaningScales numerical domain and collision coefficient
findings: The threshold substitution q=d/(100*k^3), r=d/(100*k^2) proves 4*ell*q<=r from k>0 and 4*ell<=k; no sign-reversing division is used.
For ell>=1 and d>=k^2, t=ell*d/k^2 is nonnegative, ell<=t, the collision term is <=t/100 and the two mate terms together are <=3*t/100. Thus their sum is <=1.04*t<=2*t.
cleaning_scale_nat_loss explicitly bounds the actual natural-number factor ell*(ell-1) by ell^2; it does not replace truncated natural subtraction by an unlicensed real subtraction.

cleaning_dense_scale combines n<=2*(ell+1)*D, D<=5*k*d and ell+1<=k to get n<=10*k^2*d. The retained r^2<=4*e implies d^2<=40000*k^4*e, yielding d*n/(400000*k^6)<=e. All denominators are positive under k>0.
The theorem instantiates the prior actual-graph cleaning theorem with K=5*k, eps1=1/(100*k^2), eps2=1/(100*k^3), and r=d/(100*k^2); multiplication/division conversions preserve thresholds exactly.
The dense alternative supplies a finite vertex set H in the original graph, and edgeFinset counts of G.induce H, not a scalar proxy or assumed density oracle.

Since k>0 and d>=k^2, d>0 and r>0. Its retained r^2<=4*|E(G[H])| forces positive edge count, hence at least one genuine edge and nonempty H. The multiplicative density inequality alone could admit H empty, but it is not the sole witness condition.

The other alternative uses the actual fullStarContraction simple quotient. MinorModel requires nonempty connected pairwise-disjoint branch sets and host adjacency witnesses; fullStarBranch includes all residual vertices as singleton branches. Coverage, width ell+1, original-host branch mate-freeness and the exact vertex-loss equality remain conclusions.
The actual edge loss is bounded by (2*ell*d/k^2)*|C| by multiplying the proved coefficient inequality by nonnegative |C|. The cleaned family has the same covered leaf union as the initial family.

Initial packing, full ell-sized stars, original-host mate-freeness, original covered-vertex degree bound D, D<=5*k*d, original Unmated condition, bipartition and C subset B are all explicit premises. The theorem does not construct that starting family or prove a density increment.

For a selected leaf x, packing membership puts x in A. The original bipartition puts every neighbor in B and excludes neighbors in the selected leaf union. Consequently its induced-host neighbors are exactly original neighbors in C.

The neighbor-finset partition by membership in C gives the exact natural degree identity: selected induced degree plus boundary-neighbor count in B minus C equals original degree. There is no assumption that selected centers exhaust B.
The lower bound (1-eps)*d follows from the explicit original minimum degree and boundary estimate by coercion to real numbers; no minimum-degree conclusion is simply postulated.

semantic_checks.topic: InducedStarFamily literal selected subtype and mate preservation
findings: SelectedStarVertex is exactly the subtype of C union C.biUnion L. Selected centers, leaves and assignment are literal finset subtype restrictions, rather than abstract sets with assumed cardinalities.

Assignments outside C are empty by IsStarPacking, so every assigned leaf has an actual selected owner. No assigned leaf is lost in the subtype restriction, and packing edges, independence, disjointness and size bounds transfer to the genuine induced graph.

The star branches cover every vertex of the selected subtype by a direct centers-or-owned-leaves argument. With the original bipartition and C subset B, the selected leaf and center domains are disjoint and give the exact induced-host bipartition.
Full star sizes transfer, and pairwise-disjoint full leaf sets give the exact ratio |selected leaves|=ell*|selected centers|; this is not a hidden original-right-side cardinality premise.

Mate-freeness transfers by an injective map from actual induced-graph common-neighbor subtypes to actual original-graph common-neighbor subtypes. Strict threshold q is unchanged. No global Unmated heredity is used.
The theorem requires a natural integer m with 1<=m and real m<=(1-eps)*d explicitly; it does not silently round or assert existence of a suitable m.

The exact induced leaf-degree lower bound supplies m<=host degree. The existing genuine forest has leaf degree at most one, allowing seeded neighbor selection to extend its mandatory edges to exactly m neighbors at every selected leaf.

The constructed H is on the exact selected vertex type, contains the actual selected star forest, and is a subgraph of the actual induced host. Bipartiteness yields H.edgeFinset.card=m*|selected leaves| by a one-sided degree sum, with no factor-of-two error.
between_forest retains every chosen center-leaf edge and preserves within-star independence by H<=host. Original full sizes, literal full coverage and exact leaf/center ratio remain conclusions.
Mate-freeness first transfers to the induced host via the injection, then to H by common-neighbor monotonicity under edge deletion. No global Unmated assertion is transported to the trimmed graph.

source_context.supporting_locations: Text lines 341-365 (Theorems 3.6 and 3.7), 383-397 (their distinct substitutions in the proof of Theorem 2.1), and Section 4 references beginning at line 492. These are in the supplied source context on pages 7-12.
source_context.verified_distinction: The bipartite Theorem 3.6 uses separate eps1,0 and eps2,0, with allowed upper scales 1/ell and 1/ell^2. Its cited application sets eps1,0=1/ell and eps2,0=1/ell^2. Global Theorem 3.7 instead has eps1 and eps2 and is applied earlier with both equal to 1/k.
source_context.conclusion: This conservative inverse-cubic supporting construction does not establish that the bipartite application needs a polynomial parameter change. Comparing it only to global Theorem 3.7 inverse-k parameters is insufficient. No new source defect or asymptotic repair is inferred or certified here.
source_context.outside_frozen_route: The separate outside-frozen inverse-quadratic bipartite drafts are excluded from this review and receive no certification.

caveats: The five modules prove supporting constructions under the stated domain; they do not complete the paper, full density increment, main upper bounds or the initial-family/parameter joins.

Do not drop the positive edge witness from the dense alternative, original covered-vertex degree assumptions, starting full mate-free packing, original Unmated premise, or explicit integer threshold 1<=m<=(1-eps)*d.

The selected-family theorems allow empty selected domains when the input is empty, and regularization does not itself prove a nonempty selection or a positive density increment. This is an explicit construction from its input, not an existential claim of a useful nonempty initial family. Full contraction still retains all original residual vertices.

Global Unmated is not hereditary under graph deletion because the small-vertex classification can change. A later application to the selected or regularized host still needs a separate small-dense-or-Unmated argument.
Recorded local build/audit/replay passes were inspected but not rerun; publication and exact remote-commit CI are outside this bounded review.
Keep Postle Theorem 3.6 bipartite epsilon parameters distinct from global Theorem 3.7 epsilon parameters; this package certifies no polynomial repair or new source defect.
